name: Victorian (1890)
note: 24-inch projectors with plain carbon arcs on the bridges, the fighting tops and the flying deck, to search for torpedo boats; the boats a small one or none [EST].

name: Pre-dreadnought (1904)
note: 75 cm projectors (the Russian and Japanese fleets' at Port Arthur and Tsushima), trained by hand at each light on orders by voice pipe [EST].

name: RN pre-dreadnought (1904)
note: 24-inch on the big ships, 20-inch on the destroyers, each trained at the light [EST].

name: Great War (1914)
note: 36-inch on the big ships (searchlight towers by the funnels, the bridge's wings), 24-inch on the destroyers, plain carbon arcs, each light trained by its own crew [EST].

name: RN post-Jutland (1918)
note: As in 1914, now trained from searchlight control positions with directing sights after the night of Jutland [EST].

name: German Great War (1914)
note: 110 cm on the big ships, 60 cm on the boats, worked from a searchlight control position by a drilled crew: the lights that found the 4th Flotilla at Jutland [EST].

name: USN high-intensity (1918)
note: 36-inch Sperry high-intensity arcs: about four times the plain arc's beam, narrower [EST].

name: Interwar (1930)
note: High-intensity arcs everywhere, fewer and bigger lights, trained from control positions [EST].

name: Second War (1940)
note: 150 cm (44-inch in the RN) high-intensity lights slaved to the fire-control directors [EST].
